en: The PI Agent stores all its sessions, unless
you added --nosession, of course,
in files on your system. And I got lots of
folders in that PI Agent sessions folder
because I got lots of sessions across my
entire system. Now, here's the folder for
the sessions of my course project here.
And if we take a look at such a JSONL file,
which is the file format PI uses for storing
those sessions,
we see that sessions are stored like this.
We have a list of things that happen in a
session. So when a session started, when a
model was selected, and then one line for
each message, messages by us or by the
agent, and also lines for the tool calls,
for web search results and all that fun
stuff.
And you see that every turn in that
conversation essentially has an ID
and also has a parent ID. Because PIA
organizes these sessions as trees
where each turn is related to another turn.
So this message here
has a parent ID of 9F31 and so on, which is
the ID of the message in front of it or of
the turn in front of it.
The next turn has a parent ID that looks
like this, which is of course this ID.
Now,
why does PIA do that? Why not just order
these
messages, right? I mean, they are in the
right order anyways. Why this ID logic?
Because
you can actually branch out inside of your
session and you can actually split your
session at various points and follow down
different paths and then merge together
those paths later. And that sounds very
confusing, but it can be very useful and
we'll see it in action now.
